**Kepler Laveran de Lima Ferreira** [ComM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_Merit_\(Portugal\) "Order of Merit \(Portugal\)") (born 26 February 1983), known as **Pepe** (Brazilian Portuguese: [[ˈpɛpi]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Portuguese "Help:IPA/Portuguese")European Portuguese: [[ˈpɛpɨ]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Portuguese "Help:IPA/Portuguese")is a former professional [footballer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football") who played as a [centre-back](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Centre-back "Centre-back"). He is regarded as one of the greatest defenders of his generation.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-4)
Born and raised in Brazil, Pepe moved to Portugal to sign with [Marítimo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C.S._Mar%C3%ADtimo "C.S. Marítimo"), before moving to [Porto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Porto "FC Porto") in 2004. During his first Porto stint, he won two [Primeira Liga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primeira_Liga "Primeira Liga") titles, two [Taças de Portugal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ta%C3%A7a_de_Portugal "Taça de Portugal") and the [Intercontinental Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intercontinental_Cup_\(1960%E2%80%932004\) "Intercontinental Cup \(1960–2004\)"). Three years later, he moved to [Real Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Madrid_CF "Real Madrid CF") and went on to become a mainstay for the club, winning fifteen major honours, including three [La Liga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Liga "La Liga") titles, two FIFA Club World Cup titles, two [Copa del Rey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey "Copa del Rey") titles and three [UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Champions_League "UEFA Champions League") titles, playing a crucial part in all three UEFA Champions League wins.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-5) Out of contract, Pepe signed with Turkish club [Beşiktaş](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Be%C5%9Fikta%C5%9F_J.K. "Beşiktaş J.K.") in 2017, before returning to [Porto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Porto "Porto") in 2019. In his final stint with the _Dragões_ , he won a further two league titles, four Taças de Portugal and a [Taça da Liga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ta%C3%A7a_da_Liga "Taça da Liga").
Internationally, Pepe opted to play for [Portugal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portugal_national_football_team "Portugal national football team"), representing the nation at four [FIFA World Cups](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA_World_Cup "FIFA World Cup") and five [UEFA European Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_European_Championship "UEFA European Championship"). He won the [UEFA Euro 2016](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2016 "UEFA Euro 2016") title in France, being named player of the match in [the final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2016_final "UEFA Euro 2016 final"), and was named in the [UEFA Euro Team of the Tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_European_Championship_awards#Team_of_the_Tournament "UEFA European Championship awards") in 2008, 2012 and 2016. He also won the inaugural [UEFA Nations League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Nations_League "UEFA Nations League") in [2019](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_UEFA_Nations_League_Finals "2019 UEFA Nations League Finals"). Between his debut in 2007 and 2024, Pepe earned [141 caps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_men's_footballers_with_100_or_more_international_caps "List of men's footballers with 100 or more international caps").
## Club career
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Club career")]
### Marítimo
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Marítimo")]
Born in [Maceió](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macei%C3%B3 "Maceió"), [Alagoas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alagoas "Alagoas"), Pepe was named Kepler Laveran by his father in honour to scientists [Johannes Kepler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannes_Kepler "Johannes Kepler") and [Charles Louis Alphonse Laveran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Louis_Alphonse_Laveran "Charles Louis Alphonse Laveran").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-6) He started playing football with local [Corinthians Alagoano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sport_Club_Corinthians_Alagoano "Sport Club Corinthians Alagoano"). At age 18, alongside teammate [Ezequias](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ezequias "Ezequias"), he moved to Portugal to sign with [Marítimo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C.S._Mar%C3%ADtimo "C.S. Marítimo") in [Madeira](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madeira "Madeira"), spending the vast majority of his first season with the [B-team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C.S._Mar%C3%ADtimo_B "C.S. Marítimo B").
After being promoted to the main squad for the [2002–03 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002%E2%80%9303_Primeira_Liga "2002–03 Primeira Liga"), under Ukrainian manager [Anatoliy Byshovets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anatoliy_Byshovets "Anatoliy Byshovets"), Pepe rarely missed a match, playing in several positions including [defensive midfielder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midfielder#Defensive_midfielder "Midfielder").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]
During the [2002–03 pre-season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002%E2%80%9303_Primeira_Liga "2002–03 Primeira Liga"), Pepe was given permission to train with [Sporting CP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sporting_CP "Sporting CP") for two weeks, after which a deal could be negotiated for his transfer. However, neither club could agree on financial terms and the negotiations broke down, with the player returning[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-7) and going on to help Marítimo finish sixth in the [following campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2003%E2%80%9304_Primeira_Liga "2003–04 Primeira Liga") and qualify to the [UEFA Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004%E2%80%9305_UEFA_Cup "2004–05 UEFA Cup"), having contributed with 1 goal in 30 matches.
### Porto
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Porto")]
[![](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/4/46/Pepe_Porto.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail_unscaled)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Pepe_Porto.jpg)Pepe playing for [Porto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Porto "FC Porto") in 2006
In May 2004, shortly before the club sealed the league and [UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Champions_League "UEFA Champions League"), Pepe signed for [Porto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Porto "FC Porto").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-8)
In [his first season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004%E2%80%9305_Primeira_Liga "2004–05 Primeira Liga"), with Spanish coach [Víctor Fernández](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/V%C3%ADctor_Fern%C3%A1ndez "Víctor Fernández") at the helm, Pepe was mostly used as a backup player, playing under veterans [Pedro Emanuel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pedro_Emanuel "Pedro Emanuel"), [Jorge Costa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jorge_Costa_\(footballer\) "Jorge Costa \(footballer\)") and utility defender [Ricardo Costa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ricardo_Costa_\(footballer,_born_1981\) "Ricardo Costa \(footballer, born 1981\)"). However, in [the following year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005%E2%80%9306_Primeira_Liga "2005–06 Primeira Liga"), under the guidance of [Co Adriaanse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Co_Adriaanse "Co Adriaanse"), he had a breakthrough season, establishing himself as one of the best defenders in the domestic competition: the Dutchman often chose a [3–4–3 offensive system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formation_\(association_football\) "Formation \(association football\)"), with the player often pitched as the only natural stopper.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] Porto eventually won back-to-back leagues and the [Taça de Portugal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005%E2%80%9306_Ta%C3%A7a_de_Portugal "2005–06 Taça de Portugal").
### Real Madrid
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Real Madrid")]
#### 2007–11: Transfer and rise to prominence
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2007–11: Transfer and rise to prominence")]
On 10 July 2007, [Real Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Madrid_C.F. "Real Madrid C.F.") signed Pepe to a five-year contract, paying Porto a €30 million transfer fee.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-9) On 15 March 2008, Pepe scored the only ([own](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Own_goal "Own goal")) goal in a 0–1 away loss against [Deportivo La Coruña](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deportivo_de_La_Coru%C3%B1a "Deportivo de La Coruña").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-10) Eight months later, he was involved in a fight during training with teammate [Javier Balboa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javier_Balboa "Javier Balboa")[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-11) – the defender was nonetheless called up for Real's next match, whereas the [winger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midfielder#Winger "Midfielder") was not. As _Los Blancos_ were eventually [crowned champions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007%E2%80%9308_La_Liga "2007–08 La Liga") of [La Liga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Liga "La Liga"), he delivered a [Man of the match](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Man_of_the_match "Man of the match") performance in a 1–0 win at the [Camp Nou](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camp_Nou "Camp Nou") against [Barcelona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Barcelona "FC Barcelona").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-12)
Pepe was constantly hampered by injuries throughout the [2008–09 campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008%E2%80%9309_La_Liga "2008–09 La Liga"). On 21 April 2009, he was also involved in an incident with [Getafe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Getafe_CF "Getafe CF")'s [Javier Casquero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javier_Casquero "Javier Casquero"): with the score at 2–2 and only a few minutes to play, he brought down the midfielder in the [penalty area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_kick_\(association_football\) "Penalty kick \(association football\)"), being subsequently [sent off](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ejection_\(sports\) "Ejection \(sports\)"). He then kicked Casquero twice, once on his shin and once on his lower back. When being pulled away from Casquero, he also pushed his head into the turf and stamped on him several times. In the ensuing mêlée, he also struck another opposing player, [Juan Ángel Albín](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juan_%C3%81ngel_Alb%C3%ADn "Juan Ángel Albín"), in the face and eventually received a ten-match ban, which effectively ended his season.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-13)
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3f/Pepe_y_aguero.jpg/330px-Pepe_y_aguero.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Pepe_y_aguero.jpg)Pepe chasing down [Sergio Agüero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Ag%C3%BCero "Sergio Agüero") of [Atlético Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atl%C3%A9tico_Madrid "Atlético Madrid") in 2010
In the [2009–10 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_La_Liga "2009–10 La Liga"), Pepe returned to claim his place back in the starting line-ups. On 4 October 2009, he scored his first goal in the league, against [Sevilla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC "Sevilla FC") at the [Ramón Sánchez Pizjuán Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ram%C3%B3n_S%C3%A1nchez_Pizju%C3%A1n_Stadium "Ramón Sánchez Pizjuán Stadium"), heading home from a [Guti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guti_\(Spanish_footballer\) "Guti \(Spanish footballer\)") [free-kick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indirect_free_kick "Indirect free kick") in a 1–2 loss. However, on 12 December, during a match at [Mestalla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mestalla_Stadium "Mestalla Stadium") against [Valencia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valencia_CF "Valencia CF") (3–2 win), he landed awkwardly following an aerial challenge and was stretchered off the pitch in the dying minutes of the first half. Scans later showed that he ruptured his right knee's [anterior cruciate ligament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anterior_cruciate_ligament "Anterior cruciate ligament").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-14) He went on to miss the rest of the season, jeopardising his [2010 FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_FIFA_World_Cup "2010 FIFA World Cup") chances.
For [2010–11](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_La_Liga "2010–11 La Liga"), Pepe was joined at Real Madrid by countrymen [Ricardo Carvalho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ricardo_Carvalho "Ricardo Carvalho") and manager [José Mourinho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Mourinho "José Mourinho"), pairing up with Carvalho to form one of the most efficient defensive pairings in La Liga. On 2 October 2010, _[Diario AS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diario_AS "Diario AS")_ published an article where the player was reportedly open to leave the club on a [Bosman transfer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bosman_ruling "Bosman ruling").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-15) According to the newspaper, "[W]hen he signed for Real Madrid in 2007, he sacrificed a part of his salary to pay for his huge transfer fee – this made him one of the lowest earners at the club, making €1.8 million a year."[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-16) Again, he missed several matches due to injury[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-17) and, after exhausting negotiations,[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-18) finally signed a new contract, renewing his link to the club until 2015.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-19)
Pepe spent the final stretch of the season appearing as a defensive midfielder as Real Madrid faced Barcelona four times in less than one month. On 27 April 2011, in the [UEFA Champions League semi-final first leg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_UEFA_Champions_League "2010–11 UEFA Champions League"), he was sent off for a controversial challenge on Barcelona defender [Dani Alves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dani_Alves "Dani Alves") in an eventual 0–2 home loss.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-20) However, Alves also came into strong criticism, with Real Madrid claiming the Brazilian fullback had exaggerated the incident. Additionally, sportspersons including [Rio Ferdinand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rio_Ferdinand "Rio Ferdinand"), [Michael Owen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Owen "Michael Owen") and [Rory McIlroy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rory_McIlroy "Rory McIlroy") criticised Alves' actions.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-21) The next day, [UEFA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA "UEFA") opened disciplinary cases against both clubs for a number of incidents during the match.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-22) The verdict was announced eight days later: the red card stood and Pepe therefore received a one-match ban from European competition, which he served by not playing in the 1–1 draw in the second leg at [Camp Nou](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camp_Nou "Camp Nou").[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-23)
#### 2011–17: European and domestic success and departure
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: 2011–17: European and domestic success and departure")]
On 12 July 2011, Pepe extended his contract with Real Madrid again, until the end of the 2015–16 season.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-24) In a match against [Osasuna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CA_Osasuna "CA Osasuna") on 6 November, he scored the team's second goal in an eventual 7–1 home routing.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-25) In the first match of the [Copa del Rey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey "Copa del Rey") [quarter-final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011%E2%80%9312_Copa_del_Rey "2011–12 Copa del Rey") against Barcelona on 18 January 2012, he stamped on the hand of [Lionel Messi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lionel_Messi "Lionel Messi"), who was on the ground after having been fouled.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-27) The incident drew strong criticism from the Spanish media, who also noted his coming-together with [Cesc Fàbregas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cesc_F%C3%A0bregas "Cesc Fàbregas") earlier in the 1–2 home defeat,[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-28) but he insisted that the incident, which was not seen by the [referee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Referee_\(association_football\) "Referee \(association football\)"), was "unintentional".[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-29) On 23 January, the [Royal Spanish Football Federation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Spanish_Football_Federation "Royal Spanish Football Federation") cleared him of any wrongdoing.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-30)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-31)
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a2/Pepe_at_Yankee_Stadium.jpg/250px-Pepe_at_Yankee_Stadium.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Pepe_at_Yankee_Stadium.jpg)Pepe warming up for Real Madrid in 2012
On 21 March 2012, Pepe was involved in another serious incident: after a 1–1 away draw against [Villarreal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Villarreal_CF "Villarreal CF") in which he was [booked](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_card#Yellow_card "Penalty card") and Real Madrid finished with nine players, he confronted [referee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Referee_\(association_football\) "Referee \(association football\)") José Luis Paradas Romero in the locker room area, saying, "What a ripoff motherfucker."[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-32) Two days later, he was suspended for two matches.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-33)
In the 2011–12 season, Pepe formed a formidable centre back partnership with [Sergio Ramos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Ramos "Sergio Ramos"). That campaign, he went on to make 29 appearances in [La Liga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011-12_La_Liga "2011-12 La Liga") and 45 appearances in all competitions as Real Madrid claimed their 32nd league title.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-34)
On 19 August 2012, in the [league](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012%E2%80%9313_La_Liga "2012–13 La Liga") opener against Valencia, Pepe collided with Real Madrid [goalkeeper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goalkeeper_\(association_football\) "Goalkeeper \(association football\)") [Iker Casillas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iker_Casillas "Iker Casillas") in the play that led to the visitors equalising the score 1–1 (the final result). He was subsequently taken to hospital for observation,[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-35) being released the following day.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-36) Amid feuds with Mourinho, Pepe lost his starting place to [Raphaël Varane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rapha%C3%ABl_Varane "Raphaël Varane") throughout the season and would end up getting into a scuffle with [Atlético Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atl%C3%A9tico_Madrid "Atlético Madrid") manager [Diego Simeone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diego_Simeone "Diego Simeone") from the substitutes' bench in the [2013 Copa del Rey Final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Copa_del_Rey_Final "2013 Copa del Rey Final").[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-37)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-38)
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/94/Pepe_entrenando.jpg/250px-Pepe_entrenando.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Pepe_entrenando.jpg)Pepe warming up for Real Madrid in 2016
In the [2013–14 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013-14_Real_Madrid_CF_season "2013-14 Real Madrid CF season"), Pepe had a personal career high number of goals scored and appearances made for Real Madrid, making 11 appearances in their _La Decima_ winning campaign in the [2013-14 UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013-14_UEFA_Champions_League "2013-14 UEFA Champions League"). [Carlo Ancelotti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlo_Ancelotti "Carlo Ancelotti"), the Real Madrid manager at the time, spoke of his importance saying, "We're more assured with him. He gives us confidence, personality and he helps the other players; he is very important for them."[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-39) In the [2015–16 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015-16_Real_Madrid_CF_season "2015-16 Real Madrid CF season"), Pepe made nine appearances in the [UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015-16_UEFA_Champions_League "2015-16 UEFA Champions League") and 31 appearances in all competitions. He started the match when the team won the [Champions League final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_UEFA_Champions_League_Final "2016 UEFA Champions League Final") against Atlético Madrid in a [penalty shoot-out](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_shoot-out_\(association_football\) "Penalty shoot-out \(association football\)") at [San Siro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Siro "San Siro"), [Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milan "Milan").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-40)
In his last year playing for Real Madrid, Pepe had an injury-riddled season, in which he made 13 appearances, when Madrid won their 33rd [La Liga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016%E2%80%9317_La_Liga "2016–17 La Liga")[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-41)[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-42) and their twelfth [UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016%E2%80%9317_UEFA_Champions_League "2016–17 UEFA Champions League") title, defeating [Juventus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juventus_FC "Juventus FC") in the [final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_UEFA_Champions_League_Final "2017 UEFA Champions League Final") at [Principality Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Principality_Stadium "Principality Stadium"), [Cardiff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardiff "Cardiff").[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-43)

"Beşiktaş J.K.") announced the signing of Pepe on a free transfer from Real Madrid, on 4 July 2017.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-44) His contract was worth €9.5 million in total over the two-years, plus a €4,000 bonus for each match played.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-45) On 13 August, he scored his first goal in a 2–0 home win against [Antalyaspor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antalyaspor "Antalyaspor").[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-46)

### Return to Porto
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Return to Porto")]
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9b/K%C3%A9pler_Laveran_Lima_Ferreira_01.jpg/250px-K%C3%A9pler_Laveran_Lima_Ferreira_01.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:K%C3%A9pler_Laveran_Lima_Ferreira_01.jpg)Pepe playing for Porto in 2019
On 8 January 2019, Pepe returned to Porto after over a decade, on a 21⁄2-year contract.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-49) A week later, he played his first game for Porto since 2007 in the [2018–19 Taça de Portugal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Ta%C3%A7a_de_Portugal "2018–19 Taça de Portugal") quarter-finals, winning 2–1 away to [Leixões](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leix%C3%B5es_S.C. "Leixões S.C.").[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-50) While his side ended the 2018–19 season as league runners-up on the final day and lost the [cup final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Ta%C3%A7a_de_Portugal_Final "2019 Taça de Portugal Final") on penalties to Sporting, they won both tournaments in 2019–20.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-51)
Following [Danilo Pereira](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danilo_Pereira_\(Portuguese_footballer\) "Danilo Pereira \(Portuguese footballer\)")'s exit to [Paris Saint-Germain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris_Saint-Germain_F.C. "Paris Saint-Germain F.C."), Pepe was appointed as [club captain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Captain_\(association_football\) "Captain \(association football\)") on 12 October 2020.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-52) The following month, he extended his contract to 2023.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-53)
On 11 February 2022, in a [Portuguese derby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Porto%E2%80%93Sporting_CP_rivalry "FC Porto–Sporting CP rivalry") match between Porto and Sporting CP, which ended in a 2–2 draw, Pepe was one of four players sent off after starting a brawl at the end of the match; during the course of the game, he also protested referee [João Pinheiro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo%C3%A3o_Pinheiro_\(referee\) "João Pinheiro \(referee\)")'s decision not to award Porto a penalty after Pepe was allegedly kicked in the head inside the opposing penalty area. He was later banned for two matches for violent conduct.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-54)[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-55)[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-56)[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-57)[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-58)
On 25 October 2023, at 40 years and 241 days, Pepe became the oldest outfield player to play in the UEFA Champions League, in a 4–1 [group stage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023%E2%80%9324_UEFA_Champions_League_group_stage "2023–24 UEFA Champions League group stage") victory away at [Royal Antwerp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Antwerp_F.C. "Royal Antwerp F.C."), breaking the record previously held by [Alessandro Costacurta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alessandro_Costacurta "Alessandro Costacurta") for 17 years.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-59) On 7 November, in the return fixture, Pepe headed in Porto's second goal in a 2–0 victory over Royal Antwerp, becoming, at 40 years and 254 days old, the oldest ever goalscorer in the UEFA Champions League history, breaking the record previously held by [Manfred Burgsmüller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manfred_Burgsm%C3%BCller "Manfred Burgsmüller") in 1988.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-60) On 13 December, Pepe started and scored in a 5–3 Champions League victory over [Shakhtar Donetsk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Shakhtar_Donetsk "FC Shakhtar Donetsk"), setting both his records to 40 years and 289 days.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-61)
On 12 March 2024, at 41 years old, in a match against [Arsenal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arsenal_F.C. "Arsenal F.C."), Pepe became the first outfield player over the age of 40 to play in the Champions League knock-out stage.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-62)

### 2008–2014: Naturalisation and early international career
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: 2008–2014: Naturalisation and early international career")]
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d2/Portugal_2-3_Denmark.jpg/250px-Portugal_2-3_Denmark.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Portugal_2-3_Denmark.jpg)Pepe (number 3) with [Portugal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portugal_national_football_team "Portugal national football team") during a [2010 FIFA World Cup qualifier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_FIFA_World_Cup_qualification_\(UEFA\) "2010 FIFA World Cup qualification \(UEFA\)") against [Denmark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denmark_national_football_team "Denmark national football team") in 2008
Pepe never represented his native [Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazil_national_football_team "Brazil national football team") in any youth category. However, according to the player's father, in 2006, he was contacted by head coach [Dunga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dunga "Dunga") about a possible call-up, which he declined, stating that once he obtained Portuguese citizenship, he would join [its national team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portugal_national_football_team "Portugal national football team").[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-63) He became naturalised in August 2007 and, on 30 August, was named in the Portugal squad for the first time in view of a [UEFA Euro 2008](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2008 "UEFA Euro 2008") [qualifier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2008_qualifying "UEFA Euro 2008 qualifying") against [Poland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poland_national_football_team "Poland national football team").[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-64) An injury while training for his club prevented the debut for his adopted country, which would materialise almost four months later, in Portugal's last match in the tournament against [Finland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finland_national_football_team "Finland national football team") on 21 November, a 0–0 home draw.
In the tournament's final stages, Pepe played in all of the national side's matches, scoring once in a 2–0 win against [Turkey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkey_national_football_team "Turkey national football team") on 7 June 2008.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-65) Portugal was eliminated in the quarter-finals by [Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany_national_football_team "Germany national football team").
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/08/Pepe_Euro_2012.jpg/250px-Pepe_Euro_2012.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Pepe_Euro_2012.jpg)Pepe training with Portugal at [Euro 2012](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2012 "UEFA Euro 2012")
During the [2010 FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_FIFA_World_Cup "2010 FIFA World Cup") [qualifying campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_FIFA_World_Cup_qualification_\(UEFA\) "2010 FIFA World Cup qualification \(UEFA\)"), Pepe was often used as a defensive midfielder by national coach [Carlos Queiroz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Queiroz "Carlos Queiroz"). After his serious knee injury while playing for Real Madrid, he was eventually selected for the national squad that participated in the finals in South Africa, appearing against Brazil in the group stage (0–0) and eventual champions [Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spain_national_football_team "Spain national football team") in the [round of 16](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Single-elimination_tournament "Single-elimination tournament") (0–1 loss).
Again a starter in [Euro 2012](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2012 "UEFA Euro 2012") under manager [Paulo Bento](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paulo_Bento "Paulo Bento"), Pepe opened the score in the second group game against [Denmark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denmark_national_football_team "Denmark national football team"), heading home after a [João Moutinho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo%C3%A3o_Moutinho "João Moutinho") [corner kick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corner_kick "Corner kick") in an eventual 3–2 win.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-66) He was later chosen by [UEFA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA "UEFA") as man of the match[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-67) and, in the semi-final, he was one of two Portugal players to score in a 2–4 [penalty shootout](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_shoot-out_\(association_football\) "Penalty shoot-out \(association football\)") defeat to eventual winners Spain.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-68)
In the [2014 World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_FIFA_World_Cup "2014 FIFA World Cup"), Pepe received a red card in the first half of Portugal's opening match against eventual champions Germany, for headbutting [Thomas Müller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_M%C3%BCller "Thomas Müller") late into the first half of an eventual 0–4 loss. At the time, Müller was sitting on the ground and Pepe walked back to Müller to headbutt him.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-69)[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-70) He was suspended for the following match, which Portugal drew 2–2 with the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_men's_national_soccer_team "United States men's national soccer team"), before returning to the team for the final [Group G](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_FIFA_World_Cup_Group_G "2014 FIFA World Cup Group G") fixture against [Ghana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana_national_football_team "Ghana national football team").[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-71)
### 2016–2019: European champion, Nations League title and 100 caps
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: 2016–2019: European champion, Nations League title and 100 caps")]
Pepe started in central defence in six of Portugal's seven matches at [UEFA Euro 2016](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2016 "UEFA Euro 2016"). After missing the semi-final against [Wales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wales_national_football_team "Wales national football team") with a thigh injury,[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-72) he returned to the team for [the final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2016_Final "UEFA Euro 2016 Final"), where he was named man of the match, helping his team to keep a clean-sheet in a 1–0 extra-time victory over hosts [France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/France_national_football_team "France national football team") and win Portugal's first ever international title.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-73) His performance in the final was particularly noted by [Sky Sports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sky_Sports "Sky Sports") and _[Football Paradise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Football_Paradise "Football Paradise")_ 's Juuso Kilpeläinen for being firm and disciplined.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-74)[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-75)

In Portugal's second match, Pepe went down after he was tapped on the back by Morocco's [Medhi Benatia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medhi_Benatia "Medhi Benatia"). In the BBC studio, former footballer [Rio Ferdinand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rio_Ferdinand "Rio Ferdinand") called Pepe's dive "embarrassing".[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-dive-77) Former striker [Didier Drogba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Didier_Drogba "Didier Drogba") also expressed derision for Pepe, stating "he's been doing this quite a few times".[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-dive-77) Pepe scored in Portugal's [2–1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#Uruguay_vs_Portugal "2018 FIFA World Cup knockout stage") defeat against [Uruguay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uruguay_national_football_team "Uruguay national football team") in the last 16.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-78)
On 6 September 2018 in a friendly match against [Croatia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Croatia_national_football_team "Croatia national football team") at the [Estádio do Algarve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Est%C3%A1dio_do_Algarve "Estádio do Algarve"), Pepe earned his [100th cap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_men's_footballers_with_100_or_more_international_caps "List of men's footballers with 100 or more international caps"). He captained the side and headed an equaliser from [Pizzi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pizzi_\(Portuguese_footballer\) "Pizzi \(Portuguese footballer\)")'s cross to secure a 1–1 draw.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-79)
Pepe was part of Portugal's squad for their [UEFA Nations League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_UEFA_Nations_League "2018–19 UEFA Nations League") win in [2019](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_UEFA_Nations_League_Finals "2019 UEFA Nations League Finals"). He captained the team in three of the four [Group 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_UEFA_Nations_League_A#Group_3 "2018–19 UEFA Nations League A") matches, before starting in central defence in the semi-final against [Switzerland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Switzerland_national_football_team "Switzerland national football team"). During the match, he fractured his right shoulder which led to his missing the [2019 UEFA Nations League Final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_UEFA_Nations_League_Final "2019 UEFA Nations League Final")[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-80) which Portugal won 1–0 against the [Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands_national_football_team "Netherlands national football team").[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-81)
### 2020–2024: Final international tournaments and retirement
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: 2020–2024: Final international tournaments and retirement")]
Due to [Zlatan Ibrahimović](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zlatan_Ibrahimovi%C4%87 "Zlatan Ibrahimović")'s injury, 38-year-old Pepe was the oldest outfield player at the delayed [UEFA Euro 2020](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2020 "UEFA Euro 2020") finals in June 2021.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-82) On 11 November that year, he was sent off in a goalless draw away to the [Republic of Ireland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_of_Ireland_national_football_team "Republic of Ireland national football team") in [2022 FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup "2022 FIFA World Cup") [qualification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_qualification_\(UEFA\) "2022 FIFA World Cup qualification \(UEFA\)").[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-83)
In October 2022, he was named in Portugal's preliminary 55-man [squad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portugal_national_football_team "Portugal national football team") for the [2022 FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup "2022 FIFA World Cup") in Qatar,[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-84) being included in the final 26-man squad for the tournament.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-85) He scored Portugal's second goal in a thrashing 6–1 win in the round of 16 match against [Switzerland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Switzerland_national_football_team "Switzerland national football team"); by doing so, at 39 years and 283 days old, he became the oldest player to score at the knock-out stage and second-oldest player to ever score in the tournament, behind Cameroonian striker [Roger Milla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Milla "Roger Milla"), who was 42 years and 39 days old when he scored against [Russia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russia_national_football_team "Russia national football team") in the [1994 FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994_FIFA_World_Cup "1994 FIFA World Cup").[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-86) As of 23 June 2026, he stands as the third-oldest player to score in the tournament, following [Cristiano Ronaldo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cristiano_Ronaldo "Cristiano Ronaldo")'s goal vs [Uzbekistan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uzbekistan_national_football_team "Uzbekistan national football team"), at 41 years and 138 days old.
In May 2024, Pepe was selected in the 26-man squad for the [UEFA Euro 2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2024 "UEFA Euro 2024").[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-87) In the opening match against the [Czech Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Czech_Republic_national_football_team "Czech Republic national football team"), on 18 June, he became the oldest player to feature in the [European Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_European_Championship "UEFA European Championship"), aged 41 years and 113 days.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-88) He also became one of only three players to feature in five European Championships.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-89) Portugal were eliminated in the quarter-finals to [France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/France_national_football_team "France national football team") after losing 5–3 on penalties; this marked Pepe's final game in professional football.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-90) One month after this match, on 8 August 2024, one day before the start of the [2024–25 Primeira Liga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024%E2%80%9325_Primeira_Liga "2024–25 Primeira Liga") season, he announced his retirement from professional football at the age of 41.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-91)
## Style of play
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Style of play")]
Considered to be one of the best defenders of his generation,[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_\(footballer,_born_February_1983\)#cite_note-92) in his prime Pepe was a quick, aggressive, physically strong, and tenacious defender, who was known for his work-rate, energy, and hard-tackling style of play. Due to his height, he was also an aerial threat on [set-pieces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Set_piece_\(football\) "Set piece \(football\)"). While he usually played as a [centre-back](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Centre-back "Centre-back"), he was also used as a [defensive midfielder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Defensive_midfielder "Defensive midfielder") on occasion at international level. However, despite his defensive abilities, he also drew criticism in the media due to his tendency to pick up cards, as he often showed violent or unsportsmanlike behaviour on the pitch, in particular during his time at Real Madrid, which included [diving](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simulation_\(Association_football\) "Simulation \(Association
